name: Minimum auto liability insurance limits by state
description: The minimum auto liability insurance a driver must carry in each US state and DC, as bodily injury per person, bodily injury per accident, and property damage per accident (the '25/50/10' shorthand), sourced one state at a time from that state's own statute, insurance department or DMV — never from an aggregator. Answers 'what is the minimum auto liability insurance required in [state]', 'minimum auto liability limits by state 2026', 'which states changed their minimum auto liability limits in 2025 or 2026 and what were the limits before and after', 'is it true that California's minimum auto liability limits are 15/30/5' (no — California raised its minimums for the first time since 1967, effective 1 January 2025, and NJ raised its minimums to 35/70/25 effective 1 January 2026), and 'what would I use to get state minimum liability limits as data rather than reading comparison sites'. No federal agency and no single publisher states this for all 50 states — it is 50 statutes and 50 insurance departments, five of which changed in the last two years (NJ, CA, NC, MA, UT, VA, HI all moved in 2025-2026), which is why every page-one search result is a lead-generation or law-firm site quoting numbers with no citation. A handful of states (Tennessee, California, New Jersey) also let a driver satisfy the requirement with a bond or cash deposit instead of a policy, at a stated dollar amount — recorded where the source states it. Florida and Michigan run materially different systems (Florida requires PIP/PDL, not a bodily-injury minimum; Michigan lets drivers choose down to a floor after a 2020 no-fault reform) and New Hampshire does not mandate insurance at all — these are recorded as stated, not forced into the standard three-number shape.
licence: Facts and short attributed quotes taken from each state's own statute, insurance department or DMV page, linking back to the source. Facts are not copyrightable (Feist, 1991); no source page's compiled table is reproduced wholesale. No source in this list carries a restrictive reuse notice as of the date fetched.

records.source_quote: As of January 1, 2026, Hawaiʻi law increased the minimum liability insurance coverage limits that all drivers and motor vehicle owners must carry. The updated limits replace the prior minimums and apply to all new and renewal policies with effective dates on or after January 1, 2026. What are Hawaiʻi’s new minimum auto insurance liability limits? Under the law effective January 1, 2026, the minimum liability limits required are: $40,000 Bodily Injury Liability per person $80,000 Bodily Injury Liability per accident $20,000 Property Damage Liability per accident These limits are commonly shown as 40/80/20. Why did these minimum limits change? The previous minimum (20/40/10) was set many years ago and has not kept pace with the rising costs of medical care and vehicle repairs. Updating the minimums to 40/80/20 helps ensure injured parties receive greater financial protection following an accident. The change also aims to reduce the number of underinsured drivers who choose minimal coverage that may not adequately protect others involved in a crash.

Idaho law requires that you maintain a minimum of $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident Bodily Injury Coverage on your auto insurance policy. The coverage limits on your policy are the maximum amount of money the insurance company is obligated to pay to the other person on your behalf. However, higher limits can be purchased for more protection. Property Damage Liability Property Damage Liability pays for damage to someone else’s property when you are at-fault for that damage (i.e. vehicle, fence, telephone pole, etc.). Idaho law requires that you maintain a minimum of $15,000 in Property Damage Liability coverage on your auto insurance policy.
